     9  public import Mathlib.Logic.Function.Iterate
    10  public import Mathlib.Order.Basic
    11  public import Mathlib.Tactic.Coe
    12  
    13  /-!
    14  # Monotonicity
    15  
    16  This file defines (strictly) monotone/antitone functions. Contrary to standard mathematical usage,
    17  "monotone"/"mono" here means "increasing", not "increasing or decreasing". We use "antitone"/"anti"
    18  to mean "decreasing".
    19  
    20  ## Definitions
    21  
    22  * `Monotone f`: A function `f` between two preorders is monotone if `a ≤ b` implies `f a ≤ f b`.
    23  * `Antitone f`: A function `f` between two preorders is antitone if `a ≤ b` implies `f b ≤ f a`.
    24  * `MonotoneOn f s`: Same as `Monotone f`, but for all `a, b ∈ s`.
    25  * `AntitoneOn f s`: Same as `Antitone f`, but for all `a, b ∈ s`.
    26  * `StrictMono f` : A function `f` between two preorders is strictly monotone if `a < b` implies
    27    `f a < f b`.
    28  * `StrictAnti f` : A function `f` between two preorders is strictly antitone if `a < b` implies
    29    `f b < f a`.
    30  * `StrictMonoOn f s`: Same as `StrictMono f`, but for all `a, b ∈ s`.
    31  * `StrictAntiOn f s`: Same as `StrictAnti f`, but for all `a, b ∈ s`.
    32  
    33  ## Implementation notes
    34  
    35  Some of these definitions used to only require `LE α` or `LT α`. The advantage of this is
    36  unclear and it led to slight elaboration issues. Now, everything requires `Preorder α` and seems to
    37  work fine. Related Zulip discussion:
    38  https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/113488-general/topic/Order.20diamond/near/254353352.
    39  
    40  ## Tags
    41  
    42  monotone, strictly monotone, antitone, strictly antitone, increasing, strictly increasing,
    43  decreasing, strictly decreasing
    44  -/
    45  
    46  @[expose] public section
    47  
    48  assert_not_exists Nat.instLinearOrder Int.instLinearOrder
    49  
    50  
"}]

    13  /-!
    14  # Integral over an interval
    15  
    16  In this file we define `∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ` to be `∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ` if `a ≤ b` and
    17  `-∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ` if `b ≤ a`.
    18  
    19  ## Implementation notes
    20  
    21  ### Avoiding `if`, `min`, and `max`
    22  
    23  In order to avoid `if`s in the definition, we define `IntervalIntegrable f μ a b` as
    24  `IntegrableOn f (Ioc a b) μ ∧ IntegrableOn f (Ioc b a) μ`. For any `a`, `b` one of these
    25  intervals is empty and the other coincides with `Set.uIoc a b = Set.Ioc (min a b) (max a b)`.
    26  
    27  Similarly, we define `∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ` to be `∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ`.
    28  Again, for any `a`, `b` one of these integrals is zero, and the other gives the expected result.
    29  
    30  This way some properties can be translated from integrals over sets without dealing with
    31  the cases `a ≤ b` and `b ≤ a` separately.
    32  
    33  ### Choice of the interval
    34  
    35  We use integral over `Set.uIoc a b = Set.Ioc (min a b) (max a b)` instead of one of the other
    36  three possible intervals with the same endpoints for two reasons:
    37  
    38  * this way `∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ + ∫ x in b..c, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..c, f x ∂μ` holds whenever
    39    `f` is integrable on each interval; in particular, it works even if the measure `μ` has an atom
    40    at `b`; this rules out `Set.Ioo` and `Set.Icc` intervals;
    41  * with this definition for a probability measure `μ`, the integral `∫ x in a..b, 1 ∂μ` equals
    42    the difference $F_μ(b)-F_μ(a)$, where $F_μ(a)=μ(-∞, a]$ is the
    43    [cumulative distribution function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumulative_distribution_function)
    44    of `μ`.
    45

    65  -/

    68  /-- A function `f` is called *interval integrable* with respect to a measure `μ` on an unordered
